messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in the universe is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s** (about 180,000 km). Its mass is estimated to be around 10–15 M_J, placing it at the upper end of the planetary regime before it becomes a brown dwarf.

In our own Solar System, the biggest planet is Jupiter, with a radius of about 71,500 km (≈ 11.2 R_⊕).
